- [x] I, the PR author, have personally reviewed every line of this PR.

# What does this PR do?

Bound fine-grained activation offload storage with an optional reusable pinned buffer.

Variable MoE activation shapes can grow the pinned host allocator's cache, and power-of-two rounding can substantially exceed the requested capacity. This adds `--fine-grained-offloading-buffer-size-gib` to pack backups into one fixed buffer per rank, with CUDA events protecting reuse after H2D reads. The default remains disabled.

The buffer uses `cudaHostAlloc` directly, avoiding PyTorch's power-of-two rounding: for example, a 152 GiB budget no longer requires a 256 GiB allocation. Capacity must be a positive multiple of 256 bytes; CUDA may round to whole pages. The buffer never grows and raises a clear error when exhausted. Views retain the backing allocation; captured graphs require the buffer owner to remain alive.




## Contribution process

### Pre-checks

- [x] I have added relevant unit tests
- [ ] I have added relevant functional tests
- [ ] If this PR adds or changes a GPU kernel (Triton, `jit_fuser`/`torch.compile`, CUDA extension, TE or external-library dispatch, or a scatter/index accumulation), I have added or updated its bit-exact determinism test and registered it in `tests/unit_tests/determinism/kernels/manifest.py` ([guide](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/main/docs/developer/determinism/testing.md))
- [x] I have added proper typing to my code [Typing guidelines](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html)
- [x] I have added relevant documentation

**Keep captured backups reserved during eager offloads.**

**Failure:** Capture a forward graph containing `handler.offload(source)` and a separate backward graph containing `handler.reload(state)`, using the same fixed pool. Backward capture calls `release()`, leaving `_live` empty. Then replay forward with value 17, eagerly offload another same-sized tensor containing 29, and replay backward. This branch resets the eager allocation to offset zero, so the eager copy overwrites the captured backup and backward reloads 29 instead of 17. Graph replay executes neither the Python allocation nor release bookkeeping.

This affects the supported mixed path: captured attention offloads followed by eager expert offloads. [Attention capture/replay](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/ec2acd019e8c19e34999c97df3de35a09ee2d3a2/megatron/core/transformer/transformer_layer.py#L1831-L1891) and [eager MoE execution after replay](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/ec2acd019e8c19e34999c97df3de35a09ee2d3a2/megatron/core/transformer/transformer_layer.py#L1943-L2021) share this pool. The existing CUDA-graph integration cases include `core_attn`, `attn_proj`, and `expert_fc1`, but [their builder leaves the buffer disabled](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/ec2acd019e8c19e34999c97df3de35a09ee2d3a2/tests/unit_tests/pipeline_parallel/test_fine_grained_activation_offloading.py#L987-L1034).

**Correction:** Make `PinnedActivationBuffer.allocate()` and the capture branch of `release()` distinguish graph-lifetime reservations from eager live backups. Captured addresses must remain reserved while their graphs can replay; eager epochs must use disjoint space within the same capacity and still raise on exhaustion. Backward *capture* must not make those addresses available to eager writers. The exact reservation/lifecycle implementation is not unambiguous from the current API, so I am not suggesting a one-line bookkeeping patch.

**Preservation and acceptance — proposed checks, not executed:**
- Add the split-graph sequence above: captured reload must return 17; reloading the eager state must return 29; capacity must remain unchanged.
- Enable a nonzero budget in the existing mixed attention/expert CUDA-graph integration case, with delayed offloading both enabled and disabled. Preserve its logits and gradient comparisons against the baseline (`rtol=atol=1e-2`).
- Retain graph-only replay’s `output == value` and `output2 == value`, and eager multi-reader reuse’s old values 17/29 and new value 43 in [the buffer tests](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/ec2acd019e8c19e34999c97df3de35a09ee2d3a2/tests/unit_tests/pipeline_parallel/test_pinned_activation_buffer.py#L53-L122). Eager-only epochs must still reclaim storage after all readers retire; graph-owned slots require the longer lifetime.
- Keep the disabled-buffer routing unchanged: variable MoE groups bypass the shape cache, while `core_attn` uses it, as asserted by [the routing test](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/ec2acd019e8c19e34999c97df3de35a09ee2d3a2/tests/unit_tests/pipeline_parallel/test_pinned_activation_buffer.py#L192-L207).

+"""Bounded pinned storage for fine-grained activation offloading."""

+
+logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)

+    """Return the cuda-python runtime bindings."""
+    try:
+        import cuda.bindings.runtime as cuda_runtime  # type: ignore[import-untyped]

+        raise RuntimeError("A fixed pinned activation buffer requires cuda-python") from error
+    return cuda_runtime

+    """Free a cudaHostAlloc allocation with the allocating device current.
+
+    Garbage collection may run this on any thread; selecting the device keeps the
+    runtime from creating a context on another GPU.
+    """
+    cuda_runtime = _cuda_runtime()
+    with torch.cuda.device(device):
+        (error,) = cuda_runtime.cudaFreeHost(address)
+    if error != cuda_runtime.cudaError_t.cudaSuccess:
+        logger.warning("cudaFreeHost of the pinned activation buffer failed: %s", error)
+
+
+class PinnedActivationBuffer:
+    """Pack saved activations into one fixed, reusable pinned buffer.
+
+    Allocations append within the buffer. Once all backups have been reloaded,
+    the next allocation reuses the buffer after waiting for its H2D readers.
+    Interleaved chunks share one budget; storage is not reclaimed until all
+    outstanding backups are consumed. No individual-tensor free list is needed.

+    Capacity may be any positive multiple of 256 bytes and is pinned at that size:
+    the storage comes from cudaHostAlloc directly rather than from the PyTorch

+    of two. Storage is allocated at construction and freed once this object and
+    every view of it are gone. Captured graphs hold raw addresses, so keep this
+    object alive while any graph that uses it can replay. Exhaustion raises an
+    error; the buffer never grows.
+    """
+
+    ALIGNMENT = 256
+
+    def __init__(self, capacity_bytes: int) -> None:
+        if capacity_bytes < self.ALIGNMENT or capacity_bytes % self.ALIGNMENT:
+            raise ValueError(
+                "Pinned activation buffer capacity must be a positive multiple of 256 bytes"
+            )
+        if torch.cuda.is_current_stream_capturing():
+            raise RuntimeError("Create the pinned activation buffer before CUDA graph capture")
+        self.capacity_bytes = capacity_bytes
+        self.peak_live_bytes = 0
+        self.live_bytes = 0
+        self._storage = self._allocate_storage(capacity_bytes)
+        self._typed_storage: dict[torch.dtype, torch.Tensor] = {}
+        self._offset = 0
+        self._live: dict[int, int] = {}
+        self._reader_streams: dict[int, torch.cuda.Stream] = {}
+        self._pending_events: list[torch.cuda.Event] = []
+        self._captured_events: list[torch.cuda.Event] = []
+        self._writers_waited: set[int] = set()
+
+    def _allocate_storage(self, capacity_bytes: int) -> torch.Tensor:
+        """Pin exactly ``capacity_bytes`` (rounded up to whole pages) with cudaHostAlloc.
+
+        This is the same page-locked, mapped allocation the PyTorch pinned host
+        allocator makes, without its power-of-two rounding. ``torch.frombuffer`` keeps
+        the backing object alive while any view of the storage exists, so its finalizer
+        frees the pages only after the last view is gone. The finalizer does not run at
+        interpreter exit: cudaFreeHost synchronizes the device, and process exit
+        releases the pages anyway.

+        started = time.perf_counter()
+        error, address = cuda_runtime.cudaHostAlloc(
+            capacity_bytes, cuda_runtime.cudaHostAllocDefault

+            raise RuntimeError(
+                f"cudaHostAlloc of {capacity_bytes} bytes for the pinned activation "
+                f"buffer failed: {error}"
+            )

+            logger,
+            logging.INFO,
+            f"Pinned {capacity_bytes / 2**30:.2f} GiB for the activation offload buffer in "
+            f"{time.perf_counter() - started:.1f} s",
+        )
+        return torch.frombuffer(memory, dtype=torch.uint8)

The first commit independently passed its 53 allocator cases. Existing graph replay, multi-reader reuse, and disabled-buffer routing tests remain passing. Formatting checks passed; advisory mypy diagnostics are unchanged from main.

Strict review passed: no significant issues found. LGTM.

This is a follow-up to review 5451769268 at `ec2acd01`. Both findings from that review are fixed at this head.

**What I checked**

1. **Eager offloads overwrote captured backups: fixed.**
   - **Allocator changes.** In [`PinnedActivationBuffer.allocate()`](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/90d3354fa5f16fcd7bf34d68130cf09d42084631/megatron/core/pipeline_parallel/pinned_activation_buffer.py#L117-L178), eager epochs now start at `graph_reserved_bytes`. Each capture, identified by `cudaStreamGetCaptureInfo`, gets its own range starting past any live or reserved bytes. Allocations made during capture raise `graph_reserved_bytes`. [`release()`](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/90d3354fa5f16fcd7bf34d68130cf09d42084631/megatron/core/pipeline_parallel/pinned_activation_buffer.py#L180-L205) does not shrink that reservation during capture. A captured read of an eagerly allocated backup also reserves the backup's address.
   - **Tracing the reported sequence.** I traced it through the new code with a 2 MiB pool:
     - Forward capture puts the backup at `[0, 1 MiB)`, so `graph_reserved` becomes 1 MiB.
     - Backward capture empties `_live`, but `graph_reserved` stays at 1 MiB.
     - The eager offload after forward replay starts at offset 1 MiB, so it cannot overwrite the captured 17.
   - **Test coverage.** [`test_split_graph_backups_are_not_overwritten`](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/90d3354fa5f16fcd7bf34d68130cf09d42084631/tests/unit_tests/pipeline_parallel/test_pinned_activation_buffer.py#L106-L149) checks this sequence in both its `eager` and `another-graph` variants:
     - replay reloads 17 and eager reloads 29;
     - capacity is unchanged;
     - a full-capacity request raises.

# What does this PR do?

Bound fine-grained activation offload storage with an optional reusable pinned buffer.

Variable MoE activation shapes can grow the pinned host allocator's cache, and power-of-two rounding can substantially exceed the requested capacity. This adds `--fine-grained-offloading-buffer-size-gib` to pack backups into one fixed buffer per rank, with CUDA events protecting reuse after H2D reads. The default remains disabled.

The buffer uses `cudaHostAlloc` directly, avoiding PyTorch's power-of-two rounding: for example, a 152 GiB budget no longer requires a 256 GiB allocation. Capacity must be a positive multiple of 256 bytes; CUDA may round to whole pages. The buffer never grows and raises a clear error when exhausted. Views retain the backing allocation; captured graphs require the buffer owner to remain alive.

Strict review passed: no significant issues found. LGTM.

This is a follow-up to review 5451769268 at `ec2acd01`. Both findings from that review are fixed at this head.

**What I checked**

1. **Eager offloads overwrote captured backups: fixed.**
   - **Allocator changes.** In [`PinnedActivationBuffer.allocate()`](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/90d3354fa5f16fcd7bf34d68130cf09d42084631/megatron/core/pipeline_parallel/pinned_activation_buffer.py#L117-L178), eager epochs now start at `graph_reserved_bytes`. Each capture, identified by `cudaStreamGetCaptureInfo`, gets its own range starting past any live or reserved bytes. Allocations made during capture raise `graph_reserved_bytes`. [`release()`](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/90d3354fa5f16fcd7bf34d68130cf09d42084631/megatron/core/pipeline_parallel/pinned_activation_buffer.py#L180-L205) does not shrink that reservation during capture. A captured read of an eagerly allocated backup also reserves the backup's address.
   - **Tracing the reported sequence.** I traced it through the new code with a 2 MiB pool:
     - Forward capture puts the backup at `[0, 1 MiB)`, so `graph_reserved` becomes 1 MiB.
     - Backward capture empties `_live`, but `graph_reserved` stays at 1 MiB.
     - The eager offload after forward replay starts at offset 1 MiB, so it cannot overwrite the captured 17.
   - **Test coverage.** [`test_split_graph_backups_are_not_overwritten`](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/90d3354fa5f16fcd7bf34d68130cf09d42084631/tests/unit_tests/pipeline_parallel/test_pinned_activation_buffer.py#L106-L149) checks this sequence in both its `eager` and `another-graph` variants:
     - replay reloads 17 and eager reloads 29;
     - capacity is unchanged;
     - a full-capacity request raises.
   - **Captured reads of eager backups.** [`test_captured_read_reserves_an_eager_backup`](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/90d3354fa5f16fcd7bf34d68130cf09d42084631/tests/unit_tests/pipeline_parallel/test_pinned_activation_buffer.py#L152-L167) covers this case.
   - **Earlier behaviour that must still hold.** These tests are still present:
     - [multi-reader reuse](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/90d3354fa5f16fcd7bf34d68130cf09d42084631/tests/unit_tests/pipeline_parallel/test_pinned_activation_buffer.py#L57-L88) still checks 17/29/43;
     - graph-only replay across epochs still checks `output == value`.
   - **Routing.** Fixed-buffer routing for the variable-shape MoE groups is checked by `uses_pool is bool(capacity_bytes or use_cpu_pool)` in the parametrized `test_chunk_offload_handler_gathers_low_coverage_views`.
2. **Single-quoted string literals in new code: fixed.** These new literals now use double quotes:
   - in [`OffloadTensorPool.configure_fixed_buffer()`](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/90d3354fa5f16fcd7bf34d68130cf09d42084631/megatron/core/pipeline_parallel/fine_grained_activation_offload.py#L201-L212), the fixed-buffer branches of `allocate()`/`free()`, and [`get_pool_status()`](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/90d3354fa5f16fcd7bf34d68130cf09d42084631/megatron/core/pipeline_parallel/fine_grained_activation_offload.py#L364-L375);
   - in the new buffer tests.

   The remaining single-quoted `_stats[...]` keys were already in the base code and are untouched.

**Scope and limitations**

- **No tree to diff against.** The tree reviewed last time is not available in this run (`context_path` is null), so I could not diff against `ec2acd01` directly. Instead, I checked both earlier findings against the current source. I also checked the later changes visible in the supplied diff and commits: the reworked allocator reservation logic, the docs update, and the test consolidation in `90d3354`.
- **Allocator checks.** I traced the new reservation logic through these cases, and found no corruption or overwrite in any of them:
  - eager-only training;
  - a single full-iteration capture;
  - interleaved per-microbatch forward and backward captures;
  - captured reads of eagerly allocated backups.
- **What the fix is proven by.** It rests on the allocator-level tests and source tracing. The model-level mixed graph/eager test described in the author's reply is not at this head; commit `90d3354` removed it. The CUDA-graph model builder still has no buffer-size parameter.
- **Tests not run.** This review only reads the source; I did not run any CUDA tests.

**Findings by severity:** CRITICAL: 0, IMPORTANT: 0, SUGGESTION: 0.

**Overall risk: low.** The feature is off by default (`fine_grained_offloading_buffer_size_gib=0.0`), and the disabled path keeps the existing shape/dtype cache routing.
